trad: It was as if nothing mattered to me anymore; I don't usually tire easily, but I felt exhausted—like I wasn't looking ahead, couldn't see a path forward, wasn't seeking alternatives, wasn't taking action. I felt comfortable—too comfortable, I suppose—and I think that worked against me. I was just drifting through the days, dealing with things that felt unfair and unnecessary, spending more time alone than with people, talking more to myself than to others, isolating myself—both intentionally and without realizing it. Relationships with others feel strange to me at times... I don't know... it's hard to describe, but most of them end the same way: distance, a conclusion, and then oblivion. There are moments when I won't even answer a simple message—I give no sign that I'm even here—and then I find myself feeling lonely. I’d skip work without even an excuse; I just wanted to stay home and sleep as long as possible, wake up and immediately crave a cigarette—wishing they wouldn't run out, wanting to smoke when I didn't have any, spending money I didn't have, only to get money later and spend it on what I no longer possessed. Losing the hope of meeting someone... a partner, a companion, a friend who’s there for you, an intimate presence—losing that... even that... the desire itself... Then I’m back to the same routine: waking up—if I’m lucky, I’ve dreamt something; if I haven't been too wasteful, having breakfast; looking at the mess in the house and thinking it wouldn't take much to clean or maintain it—sometimes I do, but it always ends the same way—getting ready and going to work, the commute, arriving and shifting into a different mindset where I think of nothing but doing what I’m supposed to do: performing well, being effective, charismatic, and funny—giving it my all, smiling and optimistic. Honestly, I do have fun there; I enjoy it. I think I’ve grown fond of it because it makes me forget that I feel like shit and helps me face the moment with a positive attitude. It’s not that I’m not like that outside of work, but afterwards, I’m back to feeling that way—feeling like *that*. It’s not like I say, "Oh, I feel..." Not exactly "like shit," but more like: "Oh yeah, I feel this way again—what a drag. Well, what's next? Where was I?" I stopped caring; I’d look at people I "knew" and, all things considered, felt they were doing better than I was. That didn't bother me, nor did I feel envious—our realities were different. I did question things, though—thinking, "What the hell? How do they do it? What would it take for me to achieve something like that?" I saw them with their cars and motorcycles; some were starting to build their own homes; they had friends and even partners by their sides. Honestly, I admired them. It seemed to me they had earned it and worked for it—that, in a way, they had triumphed by meeting their goals. I appreciated that—the ability to push oneself to get things done. I often heard people say I was intelligent and capable—that I wasn't like others, that I was knowledgeable, "crazy" in a good way, a well-rounded person, a problem-solver, not from this planet, built differently... Yet, despite all that—despite how they saw me and felt about me (sometimes I even sensed they admired me, appreciating my abilities or my way of thinking and seeing things)—I ended up feeling the same way regardless. When I really weighed the words they used to describe me, I honestly felt like a fraud. If that was truly how they saw or felt about me, why didn't I see it the same way? Sure, I’m good at certain things—I realize that, and I know I perform well or have a knack for them—but in the end, it all felt like a movie. I didn't feel like the world revolved around me, or anyone else for that matter; things just happened. Why do I feel like I haven't achieved anything? ...not feeling the need to abandon everything—though the thought does cross my mind now and then. I don't know, I felt strange. I’m writing this in the past tense because, by tomorrow, I likely won’t think a thing about what I’ve put down here. It would be like losing an object and suddenly—on another day, in another moment or space, or maybe even the very same spot—the memory of where it is comes back to you. Yeah... that’s it.
